what_worked: Hypothesis-testing structure with consistent median-vs-mean discipline and honest missingness disclosure throughout.
fix_next: Several category medians are materially off from reference values (Education, Marketing, Analytics, E-comm); verify computation filters and denominators.
verdict: Exceptionally well-structured argument with minor but real accuracy issues in category medians.
factual_error_detail: Slide 6: Education median shown $2,142 vs reference $2,435; Marketing $1,586 vs $2,369.50; Analytics $1,294 vs $419; Content Creation $1,254 vs $1,237.50; E-comm $155 vs $387. AI median $446 vs reference $503. Slide 9: anonymous listings stated as 130 (13.0%) vs reference 129 (12.9%)—borderline. Slide 7: Stripe share stated 64.8% of single-provider (n=981); reference is 636/1000=63.6% overall, plausible under their denominator choice but the revenue figure for Stripe is not cross-checked. Slide 10: 'Top 10: 50% of revenue' stated vs reference 49.6%—acceptable rounding.

evidence.insight: Slide 3's 39× mean-median gap framing, slide 4's growth decomposition showing 61.9% flat/shrinking, slide 6's volume-vs-unit-economics contrast for AI, and slide 8's marketplace multiple analysis all go well beyond chart description to deliver decision-useful interpretations.
evidence.narrative: Slide 2 sets up a falsifiable A/B hypothesis; slides 3–9 each test one dimension; slide 10 synthesizes with a Lorenz curve and actionable 'so what.' The arc is tight, purposeful, and lands cleanly.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 defines the question for a cold reader. Every slide carries footnotes declaring denominators, exclusions, and field names. Slide 9 dedicates an entire slide to data quality and missingness. Limitations are handled with unusual rigor.
evidence.accuracy: Core figures (total revenue, top-10 share, zero-revenue count, mean 30-day) match reference. However, multiple category medians diverge materially from reference values—Education off by ~$293, Marketing off by ~$784, Analytics off by ~$875, E-comm off by ~$232. These are not rounding differences; they suggest a filter or computation error in the category analysis.
evidence.visual: Consistent template with navy/orange palette, clear hierarchy (section tags, big-number callouts, footnotes). Log-scale histogram on slide 3 is well-annotated with median/mean markers and $0 callout. Lorenz curve on slide 10 is effective. Charts are purposeful, not decorative. Minor: some slides are text-heavy in footnotes.
evidence.ai_slop: none—the writing is specific, opinionated, and dataset-bound throughout. No generic filler or consulting language detected.
